mathematical_statement: Assume S_parent = S_EH[g_obs,kappa0] + S_matter[psi,g_obs] + S_extra[Xi,g_obs] + S_boundary[g_obs,Xi,B_ref].
implication: This is sufficient only if all non-EH terms are locally silent to first variation.

mathematical_statement: There is a stationary local branch Xi=Xi0 with E_Xi[Xi0]=0 and L_tau Xi0=0.
implication: Extra fields are not allowed to carry local source charge at the exterior fixed point.

mathematical_statement: For every non-EH metric/source coupling C_i(Xi): C_i(Xi0)=0 and partial_A C_i(Xi0)=0.
implication: Then delta_g S_extra and linear source-normalization drift vanish at the local fixed point.

mathematical_statement: All matter species couple to the same g_obs/coframe and not to independent MTS markers at leading local order.
implication: Hilbert stress from S_matter is the same source seen by clocks, orbits and PPN.

mathematical_statement: On the fixed branch, delta S_parent = delta S_EH[g_obs] + delta S_matter[psi,g_obs] + delta B_silent.
implication: If delta B_silent=0, the parent Euler equation is the EH equation with the observed matter stress.

mathematical_statement: (4*pi*G_ref)^-1 int_S Pi_M J_H = H_tau[S]-H_tau[reference] = M_Hilbert[S] on the same worldtube.
implication: This identifies the mass in the v-Poisson equation with the measured gravitational source mass.

mathematical_statement: S_boundary = S_GHY[g_obs] + exact/topological terms whose local variation and charge flux vanish for the chosen reference.
implication: No hidden boundary charge may renormalize G, M, beta, gamma, or the 2PN vector.

mathematical_statement: Parent-owned map relates areal/isotropic/reciprocal readouts so the +1/2 reciprocal 2PN coefficient is gauge/readout debt, not physical hair.
implication: The 2PN warning from 2505 is harmless only after this map is signed.

mathematical_statement: If THM2506_0 through THM2506_7 hold, MTS inherits EH local equations, Newton/Poisson normalization, beta=gamma=1 at 1PN, and no independent local fifth-force/source channel.
implication: The theorem is valid as a sufficient contract, but it is not yet a proof that current MTS satisfies the contract.
